candidate_relations.rationale: The Rupi R6 recovery amendment wraps legacy recovery through shared orchestration without reimplementing semantics, strengthening the Rupi lifecycle adapter's composition-only recovery boundary.

The install-package contract tests reject unsafe paths, managed-root escapes, malformed metadata, and incorrect content identity, strengthening the package validator's safe-path, root-containment, schema, and content-identity behavior.

The governed-ingestion operation requires explicit governed evidence selection and forbids inferring authority from names, paths, headings, identifiers, or prose, strengthening the Distiller directive's opaque-source and no-inferred-authority rule.

The repository README states that the project Steward owns semantic reconciliation and admission authority while the Distiller only produces candidates, strengthening the Steward handoff requirement for explicit project-authorized Steward authority.

The README's separation of candidate production, Steward reconciliation, admission authority, and deterministic execution strengthens the handoff specification's requirement that reconciliation dispositions do not imply Canon mutation.
The installation guide requires retrieval of one exact accepted release rather than an unpinned branch, strengthening the accepted immutable versioned local-package distribution model.

The installer-runner contract places package retrieval and release selection outside installer execution, strengthening the final plan's separation between authorized retrieval and deterministic local installation.

The P7 update proof demonstrates a second package-version update through the same installer mechanism with an auditable managed-tree diff, strengthening the final plan's single deterministic installer model.

The install-package update rule reuses the same verified installer transaction and removes old files only from proven package ownership, strengthening the final plan's deterministic local installation and update model.

The exceptional-recovery tests verify protected-root authorization, exact damaged-state binding, preserved evidence, and fail-closed mutation detection, strengthening the exceptional-recovery contract.
The independent R11 exceptional-recovery workflow runs the recovery conformance suite, strengthening the exceptional-recovery contract's separately testable protected ceremony.

The exceptional-recovery tests exercise protected recovery, changed-damage rejection, and recovery-record detection, strengthening the runtime's separated recovery planning, approval, application, recording, and replay behavior.

The admission tests verify idempotent exact retry and fail closed on mutated candidates, stale plans, collisions, and conflicting second admission, strengthening the R13 admission conformance workflow.

The live-model activation specification requires exact supplied evidence, preserves invalid raw output instead of repairing it, and treats execution as an external provider boundary, strengthening the Distiller directive's no-invented-provenance and no-semantic-repair rules.

The install-package contract keeps generic framework-managed state under .reasoning-distiller while project knowledge, authority, evidence, Canon, and integration remain outside it, strengthening the accepted local-package distribution boundary.
The installation guide's requirement to consume an exact accepted release strengthens the package-builder workflow's clean, validated release-source and deterministic package-production boundary.
